page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-16GB is a general-purpose, shared-core virtual server deployed on KVM hypervisors. The instance provides 4 vCPUs derived from an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at a base clock of 2.0 GHz, configured as 4 physical cores with 1 thread per core. It is allocated 16.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per vCPU). The host CPU architecture is x86_64, featuring 64 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache per core cluster, with support for standard instruction extensions including AVX, AES-NI, and SHA extensions, while omitting AVX-512 and AMX instructions. The server includes no bundled GPUs, no complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and no local disk storage, requiring external networked storage configurations.

Benchmark outcomes show uneven processing profiles driven by its shared AMD EPYC architecture. The instance shows strong burst single-core capability, yielding a Geekbench single-core score of 2310.0 and text processing score of 3183.0, both ranking in the top 10%. Conversely, sustained compute and memory tests show lower comparative throughput: stress-ng single-core performance scores 764.28 (bottom 10%) and multi-core registers 3006.18 (bottom 25%). Memory operations demonstrate decent small-block cached read bandwidth at 410.01 GB/sec, but drop significantly under large uncached memory operations to 34.61 GB/sec read and 14.27 GB/sec write. This memory behavior limits PassMark memory scores (1759.84) and impacts database operations (2467.66).

Given its balanced compute and memory ratios alongside shared-core allocations, this instance provides cost-effective resource capacity for workloads with moderate or intermittent demand. Workloads sensitive to sustained memory write speeds, heavy database transaction volumes, or dense local I/O may encounter bottlenecks. As a result, the instance is most appropriate for containerized cloud-native services, microservices, light CI/CD test runners, and standard web application hosting.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-16GB is a general-purpose virtual instance offering 4 shared vCPUs on an AMD EPYC 7542 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, coupled with 16.0 GB of RAM in a balanced 1:4 resource allocation. Built on the x86_64 architecture using KVM virtualization, it provides standard AVX and AES instruction sets without AVX-512. The configuration includes no onboard GPUs and no bundled local storage. In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates notable Geekbench single-core performance alongside mid-tier Geekbench multi-core and Clang software compilation throughput, but displays reduced performance under continuous compute and uncached memory operations such as stress-ng and large-block memory writes. Due to its cost-effective shared hardware profile and balanced memory ratio, it is best suited for containerized applications, microservices, non-intensive web backends, and lightweight CI/CD pipelines.
